docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: A global restaurant system with two very different earnings streams
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000119312505042609/d10k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000119312505158749/d10q.htm
Date: 2005-08-04

McDonald's operates a global quick-service restaurant system through company-operated, franchised and affiliated restaurants. At year-end2004 it reports31,561 systemwide restaurants. The business combines a familiar consumer brand, consistent service/value, purchasing scale, menu development and a large physical network.

The company earns restaurant sales from directly operated locations and rent/royalty-type revenue from franchise relationships. Franchisees bear much of the restaurant labor, food and operating investment. McDonald's may own or lease the underlying property and collect rent linked to contractual terms and sales.

Reported2004 company-operated sales wereUS$14.224 billion; franchised/affiliated revenue wasUS$4.841 billion. Franchisees' and affiliates' total restaurant sales are not consolidated revenue. Their system sales nevertheless influence royalty/rent receipts and brand economics.

Company-operated restaurant margin was15.3% in2004 versus79.3% franchise margin. Q2 2005 figures are14.8% and80.2%. These measures have different denominators and cost responsibilities. It would be wrong to infer corporate stores could instantly earn80% margins or that all franchise revenue is costless.

Company and affiliates own approximately37% of restaurant land and59% of buildings at year-end2004. Historical-cost property values may understate some market values, but no independently authenticated current appraisal is supplied. Leased property, franchise agreements and operating continuity restrict a simple liquidation approach.

Management's Plan to Win emphasizes people, products, place, price and promotion. Menu variety, extended hours, convenience, restaurant modernization and better execution have helped rebuild demand. CEO Jim Skinner is overseeing an ongoing recovery rather than a business whose operations have universally failed.

The potential investment appeal is therefore not necessarily replacing a poor operator. It may involve durable brand/franchise cash flows, better capital allocation and clearer separation of restaurant versus property/franchise economics. Those opportunities must respect the integrated system and franchisees' incentives.

McDonald's also owns developing restaurant concepts including Chipotle. A minority IPO has been publicly announced as a way to highlight that business and support focus. No eventual IPO price, complete divestiture or future restructuring plan is an established fact. The key question is what existing shareholders own after all costs, taxes and operating obligations, not just the gross value of attractive components.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Recovering profitability and disciplined capital spending
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000119312505042609/d10k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000119312505158749/d10q.htm
Date: 2005-08-04

US$ millions except EPS. Consolidated revenue includes company sales plus franchise/affiliate revenue, not all system restaurant sales.

| Metric | 2002 | 2003 | 2004 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 15,406 | 17,140 | 19,065 |
| Operating income | 2,113 | 2,832 | 3,541 |
| Net income | 893 | 1,471 | 2,279 |
| Diluted EPS | 0.70 | 1.15 | 1.79 |
| Operating cash flow | 2,890 | 3,269 | 3,904 |
| Capital expenditures | 2,004 | 1,307 | 1,419 |
| Calculated CFO less capex | 886 | 1,962 | 2,485 |
| Cash dividends | 297 | 503 | 695 |
| Treasury-stock purchases | 687 | 439 | 605 |

The operating-income trajectory shows a substantial existing recovery. Capital spending has declined from the aggressive expansion period while cash generation improves. The simple cash-flow measure is not pretax unlevered FCF and must not be confused with an analyst's independently adjusted sum-of-parts cash flow.

Reported2004 results include US$130 million asset/goodwill impairment andUS$160 million lease-accounting correction, partly offset by aUS$49 million nonoperating real-estate-partnership gain. The combined disclosed after-tax effect wasUS$172 million, US$0.13 per share. Not every accounting adjustment is a sustainable expense saving.

At December2004 debt was approximatelyUS$9.220 billion and cashUS$1.380 billion. At June2005 cash wasUS$1.5606 billion, current debt maturitiesUS$793.2 million and long-term debtUS$7.7637 billion. Total debt isUS$8.5569 billion and net debtUS$6.9963 billion, calculated.

June30 common shares outstanding are1,250,048,706. First-half2005 CFO isUS$1.7455 billion and capexUS$602.5 million. These figures demonstrate cash generation but should not be doubled mechanically without considering seasonality and annual investment plans.

The September analyst meeting reiterates high-teens return on incremental invested capital as an objective, not an audited standardized historical ROIC. A matched current cost-of-capital/maintenance-capex analysis remains missing.

The financial question is how much stable cash can be returned while supporting restaurant modernization, brand investment, property obligations and franchisee health. A transaction that increases distributions through leverage must be assessed separately from an operational improvement that raises sustainable cash flow.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_guidance.md:
Title: Strong US execution, weaker overseas markets and continued sales momentum
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000119312505145941/dex991.htm; http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mcdonalds-earns-decline-revenue-rises; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000006390805000058/exhibit99.htm
Date: 2005-09-09

Q2 revenue increased8%, approximately5% in constant currencies, toUS$5.1 billion. Global comparable sales rose2.8% and operating income rose5%, approximately3% in constant currencies.

Net income wasUS$530.4 million, US$0.42 diluted EPS, versusUS$590.7 million andUS$0.47 a year earlier. The headline profit decline includesUS$0.09 per share incremental tax expense from repatriating approximatelyUS$3.2 billion foreign earnings under the Homeland Investment Act.

MarketWatch's July21 report gives analyst expectations ofUS$0.42 EPS andUS$5.03 billion revenue. The result is therefore not an ordinary operating earnings miss. First-half figures also include a separate tax-audit settlement benefit, so an adjusted earnings series must remove favorable as well as unfavorable items consistently.

Management credits US menu variety, everyday value, extended convenience and execution. Europe remains uneven, with challenges in several major markets. Australia is strong, while China and Japan were weak in the quarter. A global recovery should not be assumed from the US result alone.

The September9 release reports August global comparable sales up3.4%, US3.2%, Europe3.6% and Asia/Pacific/Middle East/Africa4.0%. US results benefit from Premium Chicken Sandwiches, breakfast and extended hours while facing a tough comparison with the prior-year Chicken Selects launch.

Europe's improvement reflects France and Germany, partly offset by continued UK weakness. The differing markets reinforce the need for local customer execution rather than a single global financial-engineering solution.

The company says US comparable sales have been positive for29 consecutive months. That record is evidence of an operating turnaround already underway, not proof that the existing management must be replaced.

The period largely predates Hurricane Katrina's full effect. Subsequent closures, reconstruction, labor/fuel pressures and customer disruption remain uncertain. The pack contains no future September sales release or Q3 earnings.

The publicly stated longer-term objectives are3–5% annual sales growth and6–7% operating-income growth, with high-teens incremental returns. These are strategic goals, not a precise current-year EPS guarantee. A sound investment case separates those organic goals, cash distributions and any possible restructuring upside.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: Brand and franchise cash flow at a moderate earnings multiple
Source: compiled from: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/MCD?period1=1096502400&period2=1128124800&interval=1d; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000119312505158749/d10q.htm; https://www.fool.com/investing/general/2005/09/23/digesting-mcdonalds-presentations.aspx
Date: 2005-09-30

Historical unadjusted September30 close isUS$33.49. The prior-year daily history records an intraday highUS$35.03 and lowUS$27.31. Session volume is7.1384 million shares; the calculated20-session average is9.3337 million. The stock is approximately4.4% below the observed high, not trading at a crisis trough.

Using June30 shares of1.250049 billion gives common capitalization approximatelyUS$41.865 billion. Adding June net debtUS$6.996 billion gives indicative enterprise valueUS$48.861 billion before other adjustments. These are analyst calculations, not a contemporaneous purchase price or final transaction model.

| Valuation basis | Calculated result |
|---|---:|
| FY2004 reported EPS US$1.79 | 18.7x |
| Enterprise value / FY2004 operating income US$3.541bn | 13.8x |
| FY2004 CFO less capex US$2.485bn / equity value | 5.9% |
| Announced annual dividend US$0.67 / price | 2.0% |

The September23 Motley Fool article gives a then-trailing P/E17.1x versus19.8x for the S&P500, and expected five-year earnings growth8.6%. That is a dated published comparison, not an independently recomputed September30 consensus multiple. The historical-year P/E above uses a different earnings period.

A capital-structure proposal would need to value company-operated restaurants separately from rent/royalty economics. Corporate stores' accounting margins do not include precisely the same contractual rent/franchise burden borne by independent franchisees. A fair comparison must normalize those charges before claiming underperformance.

Likewise, owned property cannot simply be added to the full value of the earnings it supports. A sale/leaseback produces proceeds but introduces rent, taxes and transaction costs; a property transfer can change franchisee and creditor risk.

No independent property appraisal, segment market-rent study, current forward-consensus EPS or authenticated pre-cutoff activist target is available. The case for upside is plausibly stronger cash distributions and clearer economics, but its magnitude cannot be verified by substituting a future presentation.

At this price, underlying operational momentum already has value. The investor must distinguish a reasonably priced compounding franchise from a transaction-dependent thesis with leveraged timing risk.
docs.D05_market_worries_and_countercase.md:
Title: Management resists property restructuring as the operating recovery continues
Source: compiled from: https://www.foxnews.com/story/mcdonalds-limited-impact-from-gas-prices; https://www.foxnews.com/story/mcdonalds-august-sales-up-3-4-percent; https://www.fool.com/investing/general/2005/09/23/digesting-mcdonalds-presentations.aspx
Date: 2005-09-23

The September analyst meeting produces an immediate test of the property-value narrative. Reuters's September22 account says shares had fallen3.7% the prior day after CFO Matthew Paull said the company would not pursue a new structure for its vast real-estate assets. Options activity had increased on transaction hopes.

Management's concern is the relationship with franchisees and the integrated operating system. A transaction that creates value for one security while damaging franchisee economics, credit quality or restaurant investment may fail to create durable value for the system.

The counterargument is that existing ownership may obscure the economic contribution of high-margin rent/royalty receipts versus lower-margin corporate restaurants. Clearer reporting and capital allocation could reveal value without a wholesale breakup. The existence of a possible valuation gap does not establish the best legal structure.

Operating risks remain meaningful. US comparable-sales growth has slowed against strong prior-year comparisons. Europe is mixed and the UK faces a poor perception of the food; China and Japan have been weak. The global brand is durable, not immune to shifts in customer preferences or execution errors.

Fuel prices and hurricane disruption threaten discretionary budgets and distribution costs. North American head Ralph Alvarez tells investors higher gasoline prices have had limited sales impact, emphasizing convenience and value. This is management's current assessment, not proof that persistent inflation cannot hurt margins or demand.

Reuters's September9 report says August sales were near the low end of analyst expectations for3–6% growth. Banc of America analyst Andrew Barish nevertheless called the result impressive against the difficult comparison. A slowing growth rate can coexist with a strong two-year sales stack.

The September23 Motley Fool commentary favors the cash-generative business and announced Chipotle IPO, while noting disappointment over real estate. It is a disclosed shareholder's opinion, not a completed transaction valuation.

A constructive case should credit existing management's recovery and identify incremental capital/organizational improvements. A hostile “broken operator” narrative would contradict much of the public evidence. The principal uncertainty is whether additional value can be unlocked on acceptable terms without undermining the franchise network that generates the earnings.
docs.D06_peer_and_structural_benchmarks.md:
Title: Wendy's and Tim Hortons show the opportunity and limits of separation
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/105668/000129993305003828/exhibit1.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/105668/000095015205006300/l15276aexv99.htm; https://www.fool.com/investing/general/2005/09/23/digesting-mcdonalds-presentations.aspx; https://foodservice411.com/fesmag/flashnews/2005-09-12/news-7.asp
Date: 2005-09-23

Wendy's July29 strategic announcement proposes selling15–18% of Tim Hortons through an IPO, authorizes anotherUS$1 billion stock repurchase, increases its annual dividend25% toUS$0.68 and plansUS$100 million debt repayment. It expects to retain82–85% of Tim Hortons initially.

This is an announced plan, not a completed spin-off at this cutoff. Wendy's says its board began a strategic review in2004. Public commentary credits activist pressure, but exclusive causal attribution to one investor would exceed the company's own account.

Its July28 results show why segment separation can matter. Q2 revenue isUS$951 million and EPSUS$0.61. Wendy's US company comparable sales decline4.6%, while Tim Hortons Canada rises5.6% and US9.1%. A strong growth business can be obscured by a weaker consolidated brand.

McDonald's differs: its flagship US business is improving, not suffering the same contemporaneous sales decline. Separating an emerging concept like Chipotle is more directly analogous to the announced Tim Hortons minority IPO than restructuring the property economics of an integrated global franchise.

The September23 McDonald's commentary cites trailing P/Es of24.9x Sonic,25.9x Red Robin and30.6x California Pizza Kitchen versus17.1x McDonald's and19.8x S&P500. These are dated third-party comparisons, not fully standardized franchise-mix or growth-adjusted valuations.

Higher multiples for smaller restaurant concepts do not establish that every McDonald's restaurant or property asset deserves the same valuation. Growth runway, company ownership, rent obligations, capital intensity and risk differ.

Industry monthly sales also show dispersion. A September12 roundup reports Yum domestic comparable sales up2% for the period endedSeptember3, with Taco Bell up6%, KFC up4% and Pizza Hut down4%. Brand relevance and local execution matter even within one parent.

The useful benchmark is an analytical method: disaggregate different economic streams, value each after the appropriate costs, then deduct shared obligations and transaction friction. It is not “another chain announced a spin, therefore this stock must rise.”

No fully reconciled peer franchise/real-estate sum-of-parts model is available. The pack preserves observed market valuations and structural proposals without assigning an invented appraisal to McDonald's property or assuming management must accept a specific plan.
docs.D07_recent_event_timeline.md:
Title: Operating gains and Chipotle plans accompany property speculation
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000119312505145941/dex991.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000006390805000058/exhibit99.htm; https://www.theledger.com/story/news/2005/09/17/briefing/26173805007/; https://www.foxnews.com/story/mcdonalds-limited-impact-from-gas-prices
Date: 2005-09-22

**March2005 — annual filing.** FY2004 results document renewed sales/profit growth and strong cash generation after earlier operational difficulties. The property ownership percentages and separate franchise/company margins are public.

**July21 — Q2 earnings.** Revenue rises8% and operating income5%. EPSUS$0.42 includesUS$0.09 repatriation-tax expense. The company repurchases approximatelyUS$600 million, about20 million shares, during the quarter.

**July29 — peer strategic plan.** Wendy's announces a Tim Hortons minority IPO plan, capital returns and operating initiatives. This provides a public example of unlocking a different brand's economics but is not a completed McDonald's transaction.

**September9 — August sales.** Global comparable sales rise3.4%, with positive US, Europe and Asia/Pacific/Middle East/Africa results. The US posts29 consecutive positive months. Hurricane effects are only beginning.

**September16–17 — public stake rumors.** The Ledger reports speculation that Pershing Square bought4.9%. Neither side confirms or denies. The article's hypotheticalUS$2 billion common-stock cost is an assumption, not authenticated cash invested or economic instrument disclosure.

**September21 — analyst meeting.** McDonald's announces an intended minority Chipotle IPO and raises the annual dividend22% toUS$0.67. Management reiterates growth and incremental-return objectives. It rejects a new structure for core property assets, and the stock falls according to Reuters.

**September22 — continued meeting.** Executives emphasize menu innovation, remodeling, convenience and value. They say gasoline-price effects have been limited. Shares rebound as investors assess operating prospects and capital-return plans.

The publicly available agenda includes organic improvement, a planned minority IPO and meaningful distributions. It does not include an accepted core-property restructuring, a completed corporate restaurant IPO or a future negotiated refranchising compromise.

By September30, investors have both operating evidence and a visible stakeholder objection to simplistic monetization. A catalyst analysis should distinguish an announced company action from an external investor's unconfirmed interest or an unaccepted structural idea. No November presentation details or later campaign resolution appear here.

The shareholder return depends on both operating durability and the price paid.
docs.D08_pershing_square_context.md:
Title: Young activist manager, public rumors and limits of available exposure data
Source: compiled from: https://www.theledger.com/story/news/2005/09/17/briefing/26173805007/; https://www.fool.com/investing/general/2005/09/19/is-mcdonalds-restructuring.aspx; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/105668/000129993305003828/exhibit1.htm
Date: 2005-09-19

Pershing Square is a young investment manager with a visible activist role in Wendy's. September19 public commentary says it held9.9% of Wendy's and connects its pressure to the company's announced capital and structural initiatives. This is issuer ownership, not a verified percentage of Pershing NAV.

Wendy's own July29 announcement describes board/management review beginning in2004 and a package including the Tim Hortons minority IPO, repurchases, dividend and debt repayment. This supplies a real public precedent for constructive asset-value advocacy while limiting claims that one shareholder alone created every action.

September reports circulate a possible4.9% McDonald's stake. The Ledger says neither McDonald's nor Pershing confirms or denies the rumor. ItsUS$2 billion hypothetical purchase cost assumes common shares at market prices; it does not authenticate execution, derivatives, cash committed or a NAV allocation.

The rumor is already public information at the snapshot and is presented only as rumor. It is not converted into the answer or supplemented with a later detailed proposal. A model should still judge whether the operating and valuation evidence supports a new investment independently.

No complete authenticated pre-cutoff Pershing13F, exact current firm AUM, NAV, unrestricted cash or full derivatives exposure is recovered in this pack. Later filings cannot be silently substituted. Consequently there is no defensible numerical claim about how much of the firm is available for a new McDonald's position.

The potential toolkit includes private engagement, public advocacy, capital-allocation proposals and negotiation with management/shareholders. Ordinary majority control is not established. The company's sensitivity to franchisee relationships is a visible constraint on what an activist can accomplish.

Any use of options would introduce expiry, financing and path risk distinct from ownership of a durable franchise. No particular instrument or notional stake is assumed from the public rumor. The business may compound while a short-dated instrument fails.

The best contemporaneous lesson from the peer situation is to separate businesses with different economics and seek value-enhancing changes that stakeholders can accept. It does not justify assuming a hostile CEO campaign or a specific property transaction before an actual public plan exists.

drivers.driver: Separate restaurant operations from franchise/property economics; good management had already delivered an operating recovery.
drivers.quote: This is not a case at all where we think McDonald's is doing a bad job.

drivers.driver: Normalize corporate restaurants for market rent and franchise fees to reveal true economics.
drivers.quote: McOpCo, as a wholly owned subsidiary, is not achieving its full business and financial potential.

drivers.driver: Original November plan proposes65% McOpCoIPO andUS$14.7bn property-backed borrowing for repurchases; not simply a REIT spin.
Adapt means to stakeholder constraints, later withdrawing the IPO demand in favor of management actions/refranchising rather than insisting on the initial transaction.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: Eight documents. PublicSeptember stake speculation necessarily exists before requested cutoff but remains unconfirmed and cannot reveal later instrument/thesis. Primary2002–04/June2005 financials and franchise margins, historical prices, management objections and peer plan. Exact original premium, current firm NAV/13F, independent property appraisal and forward consensus remain gaps.

valuation.downside_case: Limited to 18-19x P/E on core earnings if restructuring is rejected

drivers.driver: A dominant global franchisor with high-margin royalty streams and significant real estate ownership [D01].
The market misprices the company by failing to value the ~37% land and ~59% building ownership separately from the operating business [D01, D05].
We were able to acquire our stake at an attractive 18.7x trailing P/E for a free-cash-flow-generative business [D04].
Significant opportunity exists to unlock value by separating the high-margin royalty business from the lower-margin company-operated segment [D01, D07].

kill_criteria: Comparable store sales growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters [D03].
Management pursues large, debt-funded acquisitions that dilute the franchise quality [D02].
Operating margins in the company-operated segment degrade further due to cost pressures [D01].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A sustained deterioration in comparable store sales or evidence that the core franchise brand has permanently lost its competitive moat.
final.memo:
McDonald's is a dominant global quick-service restaurant system that combines a powerful brand with a unique, high-margin royalty-based franchise model [D01]. With 31,561 locations and 29 consecutive months of positive US comparable sales, the business remains exceptionally predictable and free-cash-flow-generative [D01, D03]. Despite its scale, the company maintains a robust balance sheet with $1.56 billion in cash, allowing for consistent capital returns to shareholders [D02, D07].

We believe the market significantly undervalues the business by failing to separate the intrinsic value of its real estate assets from the restaurant operations [D05, D07]. While management has explicitly rejected a property restructuring, we see this as an opportunity to engage and advocate for a strategy that unlocks the hidden value in the company’s ownership of ~37% of its land and ~59% of its buildings [D01, D05, D07]. The current structure obscures the fact that the franchise business earns margins of 80.2%, far exceeding the 14.8% margins of the company-operated segment [D01].

At an entry multiple of 18.7x trailing earnings, we are purchasing a premier franchise at an attractive valuation [D04]. Based on 6-7% operating income growth and the potential for a re-rating toward a 20x multiple upon structural improvement, we anticipate a high rate of return for our investors [D03, D04]. Downside risk is well-protected by the business’s strong cash flow and dividend yield, which provide a valuation floor even in the absence of an immediate restructuring [D01, D02, D07].

We intend to act as catalysts for this transformation by filing a 13D and launching a public campaign to outline the benefits of a REIT or spin-off structure [D05, D08]. Our experience in similar restaurant sector turnarounds provides us the conviction that structural, shareholder-friendly capital allocation is the correct path forward [D06, D08]. We are establishing a 15% target position, reflecting our high confidence in the business quality and the value-unlock thesis [D04, D08].

valuation.eps_path: 6-7% operating income growth driven by franchise mix shift and operational efficiency
valuation.downside_case: Stagnation at 15-16x earnings if real estate optimization is ignored; strong FCF protects capital.

drivers.driver: McDonald's is a dominant, global, free-cash-flow-generative consumer franchise with high-margin royalty-like franchise fees.
The market misprices the business as a slow-growth operator, ignoring the immense value hidden in its vast real estate portfolio.
Management's current focus on operational 'Plan to Win' metrics ignores the superior returns available through a more capital-light, franchised model.
A transition to a franchised model could expand margins from ~15% to 80%+ at the unit level, driving significant EPS growth.
We have identified clear catalysts to unlock value, including a potential real estate spin-off or REIT conversion.

kill_criteria: Management explicitly rejects the franchise-first strategy and doubles down on capital-intensive company-operated expansion.
System-wide same-store sales decline for two consecutive quarters, signaling brand erosion.
Regulatory or tax changes make the tax-efficient separation of the real estate portfolio unfeasible.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the real estate is not separable or that the tax cost of unlocking the portfolio exceeds the intrinsic value gain.
final.memo:
McDonald's represents a quintessential high-quality, dominant global franchise, operating 31,561 locations with unmatched consumer brand power and purchasing scale [D01]. The business is exceptionally free-cash-flow-generative, yet its true potential is obscured by a capital-intensive company-operated model that currently generates only 14.8% margins compared to 80.2% in its franchise business [D01, D02].

The market opportunity exists because investors perceive McDonald's as a mature, slow-growth restaurant operator, failing to value the significant embedded real estate portfolio [D01, D05]. While management has made progress with its 'Plan to Win' strategy, the market remains skeptical of management's willingness to depart from a capital-intensive model that depresses overall returns [D01, D05].

We acquired our stake at approximately 18.7x 2004 earnings, a valuation that we believe is attractive given the potential for structural transformation [D04]. With 6-7% operating income growth supported by a mix shift toward franchising and disciplined capital allocation, we expect a high rate of return as the market re-rates the company from a restaurant operator to a capital-light royalty business [D02, D03].

Our role is to serve as a catalyst for value creation, actively advocating for a separation or REIT conversion of the real estate assets [D05]. We intend to engage with the board to accelerate the transition to a franchise-first model, which would permanently improve the firm's capital-light characteristics and margin profile [D01, D05].

The primary risk is management entrenchment regarding their current capital-intensive structure, which would limit the upside of our thesis [D05]. However, given the strength of the underlying cash flows and the clear path to value creation, we believe the downside is bounded [D02, D03].

We are initiating a position with an initial target of 8% of NAV, with the intent to scale to 15% as we confirm management's alignment with a value-maximizing strategy [D04, D08]. The company's high liquidity allows for efficient accumulation of this position [D04].
